paragraphs.source_en: One arrow after another flew toward the target in the pine grove ten ken away, until only seven or eight remained. paragraphs.source_en: Just as he had learned strategy and tactics from Hideyoshi while suffering under Shingen's threat, Ieyasu was now learning from Hideyoshi the art of winning men's hearts and the subtleties of statecraft. paragraphs.source_en: Anxiety stirred in Ieyasu's heart. After Lord Nobunaga's death, Hideyoshi had won the hearts of the realm's daimyō in a remarkably short time. After several years, then, his adopted sons might be willing to take the lives of their natural fathers for Hideyoshi's sake. Thus Ieyasu sometimes imagined that one day Ogimaru might turn his bow and arrows against him.
